finding.summary: Terminal receipt write is outside the enforced root byte budget.
finding.mechanism: The source permits BaseBytes+WrittenBytes <= 134217728 and then promotes staging. The same root contains run-terminal-memory-v1.json, written afterward by the parent with no root-budget reserve or byte check. A successful or refused stream can leave less free root budget than this nonempty terminal document, so this write can exceed the hard 128MiB root cap. No actual cap overrun is claimed; this is a source-level reachable boundary defect.
finding.history: The parent write pattern also exists in the predecessor command; it is not a regression attributed to the memory algorithm. The current scoped run still promises a hard whole-root cap.
finding.requested_repair: Make final terminal evidence fit within the same hard root cap, including success, source refusal and staging retention. Reserve a bounded terminal allowance before allowing payload writes and enforce actual encoded terminal length/root budget before writing, or an equivalent explicit bounded design. Keep useful terminal failure evidence without a cap increase, automatic retry, deletion, alternate output destination or weakening input/validation checks.
finding.validation: One narrow C-only boundary check of a nearly full output budget must show no cap excess and an explicit terminal outcome, on both completion and refusal paths. Recheck changed budget/terminal code and pins only; do not repeat the accepted scale/lifetime/byte suite unless an actual change affects it. Any new execution retains Leo's applicable authorization, limits and host review.
